summary: Can the nodes of an undirected graph be 2-coloured so no edge joins same-coloured nodes?
mainInsight: Colour with BFS or DFS: give a start node colour 0, colour its neighbours with the opposite colour, and fail if you meet a neighbour already coloured the same. Repeat from every uncoloured node because the graph may be disconnected. Equivalent: the graph has no odd-length cycle.

approaches.name: BFS colouring
approaches.summary: Colour levels alternately; check each edge.

approaches.name: Union find
approaches.summary: Union a node's neighbours; fail if a node shares a set with a neighbour.

commonMistakes: Not comparing against already coloured neighbours

cards.answer: Two-colour the graph with BFS or DFS from every unvisited node, failing on an edge between same-coloured nodes. Clue: Bipartite means the nodes split into two groups with every edge between the groups, which is two-colouring: neighbours must get opposite colours, and the graph may be disconnected.
keyPoints: Bipartite means the nodes split into two groups with every edge between the groups, which is two-colouring: neighbours must get opposite colours, and the graph may be disconnected.
cards.explanation: Colouring a node's neighbours with the opposite colour either succeeds everywhere or hits an edge inside one group, which means an odd cycle.

promptVariants: What property does a bipartite graph satisfy in terms of cycles?
options: It contains no cycle of any length
Every node has an even degree
It is connected and has exactly V - 1 edges
cards.explanation: An odd cycle forces two adjacent nodes to share a colour.

incorrectOptionExplanations.It contains no cycle of any length: Even cycles are allowed (e.g. a square).
incorrectOptionExplanations.It is connected and has exactly V - 1 ed: That describes a tree, which is only one case.

promptVariants: Why must the colouring be started from every uncoloured node?
What does the traversal check on each edge?
cards.answer: The graph may have several connected components and each needs its own colouring. For an edge (u, v): if v is uncoloured give it the opposite colour of u and continue; if v already has the same colour as u, an odd cycle exists and the answer is False.
cards.explanation: Starting only from node 0 misses other components.
Every node and edge is visited once.

cards.answer: No: an odd cycle forces two adjacent nodes to share a colour
cards.explanation: Nodes 0, 1, 2 mutually adjacent need three colours.
